notYet: Not yet part of the Mediterranean world

stages.name: Independent peoples
stages.desc: Italic, Iberian, Numidian and other peoples outside the great powers

stages.name: Persian Empire
stages.desc: Still ruled by the Great King Darius III and his satraps

stages.name: Conquered by Alexander
stages.desc: Taken by Alexander or under Macedonian rule

stages.name: Carthaginian
stages.desc: Carthage's city, its African lands and its island possessions

stages.name: Greek West
stages.desc: Independent Greek cities: Cyrene, south Italy and Sicily

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: The Cypriot kings abandon Persia and bring their ships to the siege of Tyre
Cyprus is to build ships for the planned fleet of a thousand

states.name: Israel
timeline: The coast and hills of Palestine pass to Alexander on his march to Egypt

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Gaza resists for two months; the city is stormed and its men killed

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Byblos and Sidon submit; Tyre falls in summer after a seven-month siege
Phoenician shipyards are ordered to build warships for the west

states.name: Syria
timeline: Syria held by Alexander after Issus; Parmenion secures Damascus
The army crosses the Euphrates at Thapsacus on the march to Persia

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Anatolia conquered in 334–333, after the Granicus and Issus
Cilicia's shipyards are named in Alexander's plans for a western fleet

states.name: Spain
timeline: Iberian and Celtic peoples; Phoenician Gadir and the south coast trade with Carthage
Iberians reportedly send envoys to Babylon

states.name: Libya
timeline: Greek Cyrene and its sister cities; the Tripolitanian coast is Carthaginian
Cyrene sends gifts and makes a treaty of friendship with Alexander

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage takes in Tyrian women and children evacuated before the siege
Carthage sends Hamilcar Rhodanus to Alexander's court as a spy
Hamilcar returns after Alexander's death and is put to death by his city

states.name: Greece
timeline: Macedon and the Greek cities of the League of Corinth under Antipater
Antipater crushes King Agis III of Sparta at Megalopolis
The Exiles Decree is proclaimed at Olympia; Harpalus flees to Athens
News of Alexander's death: Athens leads the Greeks into the Lamian War

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Mesopotamia and Babylon, heart of Darius III's empire
Darius is defeated at Gaugamela; Babylon opens its gates
The army mutinies at Opis and is reconciled
Alexander receives western embassies and dies at Babylon in June

states.name: Italy
timeline: Alexander of Epirus, Alexander's uncle, fights for Tarentum and the Greek cities
Alexander of Epirus is killed at Pandosia by Lucanians and Bruttians
Rome goes to war with the Samnites; the Greek cities lose their protector
Bruttians, Lucanians and Etruscans reportedly send envoys to Babylon

states.name: Iran
timeline: Persis, Media and the Iranian plateau, the Persian homeland
Persepolis is taken and burned; Darius is murdered by his own nobles
Alexander returns through the Gedrosian desert with heavy losses
The mass weddings at Susa; Hephaestion dies at Ecbatana

states.name: Algeria
timeline: Numidian and Moorish peoples; small Carthaginian trading posts on the coast

states.name: Jordan
timeline: The lands east of the Jordan pass to Macedonian governors of Syria

states.name: Egypt
timeline: The Persian satrap Mazaces surrenders Egypt without a fight
Alexandria is founded; Alexander visits the oracle of Ammon at Siwa

states.name: Malta
timeline: Phoenician Malta, a Carthaginian island base on the sea route west

events.title: Sidon submits
events.text: Sidon and Byblos open their gates, and their fleets join Alexander.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: Alexander builds a mole out to the island city of Tyre, which holds out for seven months.

events.title: Cypriot fleet
events.text: The kings of Cyprus bring about 120 ships to Alexander, tipping the naval balance at Tyre.

events.title: Refugees to Carthage
events.text: Tyre ships many of its women and children to its daughter city Carthage.

events.title: Tyre falls
events.text: Tyre is stormed in summer; thousands are killed or crucified and some 30,000 sold into slavery.

events.title: Envoys spared
events.text: Carthaginian envoys found in the temple of Melqart are spared; Curtius says Alexander declared war on Carthage.

events.title: Siege of Gaza
events.text: Gaza resists for two months before it is stormed; its men are killed and its people enslaved.

events.title: Egypt submits
events.text: The Persian satrap Mazaces hands Egypt to Alexander without a battle.

events.title: Alexandria founded
events.text: Alexander lays out a new city on the coast west of the Nile delta.

events.title: Oracle of Siwa
events.text: Alexander crosses the desert to the oracle of Ammon, who hails him as son of the god.

events.title: Cyrene's embassy
events.text: Greek Cyrene, Carthage's neighbour, sends gifts and makes a treaty of friendship with Alexander.

events.title: Hamilcar the spy
events.text: Justin says Carthage sent Hamilcar Rhodanus, who posed as an exile and reached the king through Parmenion.

events.title: Death at Pandosia
events.text: Alexander of Epirus, the king's uncle, is killed fighting Lucanians and Bruttians in southern Italy.

events.title: Euphrates crossed
events.text: The army crosses the Euphrates at Thapsacus on bridges of boats.

events.title: Gaugamela
events.text: On 1 October, Alexander defeats Darius III's grand army on the plain near Arbela.

events.title: Babylon opens
events.text: The satrap Mazaeus surrenders Babylon, and Alexander enters the city in triumph.

events.title: Megalopolis
events.text: Antipater defeats King Agis III of Sparta, ending the Greek revolt (331 or 330).

events.title: Persian Gates
events.text: Alexander forces the mountain pass held by the satrap Ariobarzanes.

events.title: Persepolis burned
events.text: The palaces of the Persian kings are looted and then set on fire.

events.title: Darius murdered
events.text: Fleeing east, Darius III is killed by his own satrap Bessus.

events.title: Parmenion killed
events.text: Alexander's old general, Hamilcar's go-between, is executed at Ecbatana after his son's trial.

events.title: Privernum taken
events.text: Rome captures the Volscian town of Privernum, tightening its grip on Latium.

events.title: Fregellae
events.text: Rome plants a colony at Fregellae on the Samnite frontier.

events.title: Neapolis besieged
events.text: Rome besieges the Greek city of Palaeopolis at Naples, a quarrel that leads to war.

events.title: Samnite War
events.text: Rome and the Samnites begin a war for central Italy that lasts twenty-two years.

events.title: Gedrosian desert
events.text: Returning from India, Alexander's army loses many lives crossing the Makran desert.

events.title: Nearchus' voyage
events.text: Alexander's admiral Nearchus brings the fleet from the Indus to the Strait of Hormuz.

events.title: Pytheas sails
events.text: Around this time Pytheas of Massalia sails past Carthage's Pillars of Heracles to Britain.

events.title: Susa weddings
events.text: Alexander and some ninety companions marry Persian and Median noblewomen.

events.title: Exiles Decree
events.text: At the Olympic Games, Alexander orders the Greek cities to take back their exiles.

events.title: Harpalus flees
events.text: Alexander's treasurer flees with stolen silver and ships to Athens.

events.title: Opis mutiny
events.text: The Macedonian veterans mutiny at Opis, then are reconciled at a great banquet.

events.title: Hephaestion dies
events.text: Alexander's closest friend dies at Ecbatana; the king plans a vast funeral pyre.

events.title: Envoys from the West
events.text: Libyans, Bruttians, Lucanians and Etruscans, and reportedly Carthaginians and Iberians, come to Babylon.

events.title: A harbour for 1,000
events.text: Alexander digs a harbour at Babylon for a thousand warships, for a campaign against Arabia.

events.title: Phoenician shipyards
events.text: Warships are built in Phoenicia and carried in pieces overland to the Euphrates.

events.title: Death in Babylon
events.text: After days of fever, Alexander dies in Nebuchadnezzar's palace on 10 or 11 June, aged thirty-two.

events.title: Last plans read
events.text: Perdiccas reads out the king's plans, including a thousand ships against Carthage; the army rejects them.

events.title: Hamilcar executed
events.text: Back home, Justin says, Hamilcar is put to death by Carthage on the charge of selling the city to the king.

events.title: Lamian War
events.text: Athens leads the Greeks in revolt against Macedon as soon as Alexander's death is known.

eras: To the ends of the earth

metrics.label: Beyond his reach in the west

chartNote: Share of the area of 17 present-day countries from Spain to Iran, by the power that held most of each. Regions are today's boundaries; the map is a simplification: Italy held Romans, Samnites, Greek cities and Carthaginian Sicily and Sardinia at once, and Spain's coast traded with Carthage. Alexander's campaigns in Central Asia and India lie east of the map.
